response.sql:
WITH account_order_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    o.account_id,
    COUNT(*) as order_count
  FROM `order` o
  GROUP BY o.account_id
),
avg_orders AS (
  SELECT 
    AVG(order_count) as avg_order_count
  FROM account_order_counts
),
results AS (
  SELECT 
    aoc.account_id,
    d.A3 as region,
    aoc.order_count,
    aoc.order_count - avg.avg_order_count as diff_from_avg,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY aoc.order_count - avg.avg_order_count DESC) as dense_rank
  FROM account_order_counts aoc
  JOIN account a ON aoc.account_id = a.account_id
  JOIN district d ON a.district_id = d.district_id
  CROSS JOIN avg_orders avg
)
SELECT 
  account_id,
  region,
  order_count,
  diff_from_avg
FROM results
WHERE dense_rank <= 10
ORDER BY diff_from_avg DESC;

assumptions.assumption: DENSE_RANK <= 10 selects top-10 ranking positions inclusive of all tied accounts at position 10. This interpretation matches the request phrasing 'top 10 plus every account tied with the 10th-place value', which explicitly requires including ties.
Average order count is computed only over accounts that have at least one order (those appearing in the order table), matching the phrase 'all accounts that have orders'.
